tagline: Dimension elements on reference detail lines (they stay when elements are deleted but no longer update when elements move), merge strings, and audit, rebuild, merge or re-type dimensions across views and sheets.
description: One palette for dimensions (replaces Dimension with Line and Dimension Merge). IN THIS VIEW: Cut through elements (draw a line through walls, joinery, furniture, fixtures, regions and every face it cuts is dimensioned on reference detail lines; string after string until Esc), Selected elements along a picked baseline, Rebuild existing dimensions on detail lines, and Merge 2+ strings into one (parallel strings can snap onto the first one's line). ACROSS VIEWS AND SHEETS: this view, views you pick, views on sheets you pick, views using templates you pick, or the whole project: Audit (typed-over values, zero segments, added text, locked/EQ, views hiding dimensions; clear typed values from the report), Merge in-line strings, Rebuild all on detail lines, Change dimension type. PROJECT: dimension types with use counts, replace one with another everywhere, purge the unused. A dimension on detail lines keeps its measurement when the elements are deleted but no longer updates when they move. Rebuild only restyles reference lines this tool drew; dimensions on lines someone else drew are left as drawn. Batch runs and merges are one Ctrl+Z; Cut through is one Ctrl+Z per string. Borrowed elements are skipped and named. 3D views and sheets cannot host detail lines; Cut through also measures the elements of loaded linked models.

name: Update Schedule
tagline: Export element parameters or editable schedules to a spreadsheet, then import the edited values back.
description: Four workflows. Export Elements writes every instance of the categories you pick, with the parameters you pick. Export Editable Schedules writes one worksheet per schedule, carrying only the fields that map to a writable parameter - a calculated field cannot round-trip, so it is left out rather than exported and silently dropped. The two import buttons read a .xlsx or .csv back and write the values onto the matched elements, in one undoable step; a blank cell is skipped, never used to clear a parameter. Schedule imports also match each worksheet back to its schedule and can create copies named after the original schedule with an Imported suffix.

name: Sheet Manager
tagline: Duplicate sheets, renumber and rename sheets, set sheet parameters and the title block, and add or remove revisions on sheets, many sheets at once, from one list.
description: One window for working on many sheets. It lists every sheet and placeholder sheet with its number, name, title block, current revision, view count and Appears In Sheet List; search it, filter sheets or placeholders, and tick the sheets to work on. Four tabs act on the ticked sheets: DUPLICATE: duplicate sheets 1 to 9 times, sheet only (title block, sheet parameters and sheet annotations) or with their views duplicated, duplicated with detailing or as dependent views, placed at the same spot with the same viewport type. Legends and schedules are placed again as they are. RENUMBER / RENAME: renumber sheets and rename sheets with find and replace, prefix, suffix, tokens and a sequence number (start, step, padding), with a live preview and a clash check. Swapped or shifted numbers are handled. SET PARAMETER: set a sheet parameter, Appears In Sheet List, or change the title block type on every ticked sheet. REVISIONS: add or remove revisions on sheets (Revisions on Sheet). Revisions that come from a revision cloud on the sheet are reported. Each run is one Undo step, and anything skipped or blocked (borrowed by another user) is listed in the result.

name: VP Manager
tagline: Viewport manager: align viewports across sheets, match the viewport crop, renumber detail numbers, set the title on sheet, change the viewport type, pin viewports and move a viewport to another sheet, many viewports at once, from one list.
description: One window for working on many viewports. It lists every viewport in the project with its sheet, detail number, view, view type, scale, viewport type, title on sheet, pinned and crop state; search it, filter by sheet or view type, and tick the viewports to work on. Double-click a row to open its sheet with the viewport selected. Four tabs act on the ticked viewports: ALIGN: align viewports to a reference viewport: the same position on every sheet (typical plans in the same spot), by model coordinates, or to an edge or centre of the reference on the same sheet. Optionally match the crop and the viewport type. Pinned viewports are unpinned for the move and pinned again. CROP: match the viewport crop to the reference (scope box or crop shape), grow or shrink the crop by a margin in project units or paper millimetres, and switch the crop region and annotation crop on or off. TITLES AND NUMBERS: change the viewport type (view title), renumber detail numbers per sheet left to right or top to bottom with a start number, prefix and step, and set the Title on Sheet with find and replace, prefix, suffix and tokens. PIN AND MOVE: pin viewports, unpin viewports, and move viewports (legends too) to another sheet at the same spot, keeping the viewport type, rotation, title position and detail number. Each run is one Undo step, and anything skipped or blocked (borrowed by another user) is listed in the result.
capabilities: One window for working on many viewports.

One undoable step.

name: Detail View
tagline: Wall sections plus ceiling, floor and wall detail callouts, on every cut line you draw.
description: Draw straight detail lines where you want the sections to cut, then run this: for every selected level and every picked line it creates a wall section plus its ceiling, floor and wall detail callouts. Each line's ends set where its section cuts and its length sets how wide every view is. Bottom and top heights are set per detail in mm from the level, and each can pin its own level instead. Section and callout types are yours to choose, and a head override is applied through an isolated copy of the view type so other views are untouched. Switch off any detail you do not need. The lines are removed for you and one Ctrl+Z brings back both the lines and the views.

name: Room to View
tagline: Create a floor plan, a ceiling plan and four elevations for one room.
description: Pick a room and generate any combination of its floor plan, reflected ceiling plan and four interior elevations (N/E/S/W) from one tabbed dialog. Each view type gets its own crop-to-room option with a margin you set, its own drawing scale and its own view template. Views are named from the room number and name so they are easy to find, and the whole batch is one undo step. The elevation marker is auto-swapped to a four-arrow type when the project default is single-direction - the reason all four sides used to fail.

tagline: Convert, duplicate, apply view templates to, batch rename and hide elements in many project views at once, from one list.
description: One window for working on many views. It lists every project view with its type, level, scale, view template and sheet; search it, filter it by view type or by placed/unplaced on sheets, and tick the views to work on. Three tabs act on the ticked views: CONVERT: floor plans, ceiling plans, sections, elevations and detail views to drafting views (model geometry through a DWG round-trip, rebuilt as native detail lines and filled regions); drafting views to legends, using a template legend you choose (New legend... opens Revit's New Legend dialog when the project has none); legends to drafting views; floor plans to ceiling plans (reflected ceiling plan, RCP) and ceiling plans to floor plans, with the cut plane height asked for each run (2300 mm / 1200 mm by default), a view template, and make-copies or convert-in-place, which keeps the sheet viewport. A preview lists the new view names first. MANAGE: duplicate views (duplicate, with detailing, or as dependent), apply a view template, and batch rename with find and replace, prefix, suffix and ignore case, with a live preview. HIDE IN VIEWS: hide or unhide the elements selected in Revit, or their whole categories, in all the ticked views at once. Each run is one Undo step, and anything skipped or failed is listed in the result. Replaces View to Drafting, Drafting Legend, View Type Converter and Hide in Views.
